queue.title: Crouch-look camera pan ($307D: B+Down / B+Up, 1 px/frame, edge-gated)
queue.note: Verified missing 2026-10-13: $0F71's FIRST call, and the port neither implements it nor flags it. Gated on sSceneState == 0 and (sMarioOnGround | sMarioOnObject); hKeysHeld $82 (B+Down) pans camY +1/frame while sMarioScreenY >= $20 and not (edge bit3 and camY_lo >= $C0); $42 (B+Up) pans camY -1/frame while sMarioScreenY < $70 and not (edge bit2 and camY_lo < $49). Uses the same sScreenEdgeMap as the follow, so it needs the extracted table too. The capture field named `pan` is sCameraPanTimer ($A2B3), which $307D never writes - it is NOT this feature's flag. The real evidence that the gate was blind: across the original 16 captures (~49k frames) no frame holds B+Down or B+Up while grounded. KEY LAYOUT (ReadJoypad $1FD2, verified 2026-10-13): hKeysHeld = directions in bits 4-7 (bit7 Down, bit6 Up, bit5 Left, bit4 Right) and actions in bits 0-3 (bit1 B, bit0 A, bit2 Select, bit3 Start) - so $82 is exactly Down+B, $42 exactly Up+B, and $08 (the $287E START wait) is Start. Because `cp` is exact, Select or Start held CANCELS the pan; the port cannot express those bits yet, so this becomes a live dependency of the pause item (pause_and_palette_flash) - when a START bit lands, the pan gate must include it. DONE 2026-10-13: CameraSim::crouch_pan (13 unit tests, cargo test 84) plus captures/crouch_pan1.json (508 records, $05E4-hook-sampled). That capture holds B+Down for 79 grounded frames and B+Up for 80, with 41 camy +1 steps, 41 -1 steps and 75 guard-blocked frames (camy 406-448); the port replays it ALL-ZERO on all 507 compared frames, so both pan arms and both guards match the console. Added to the README gate list.

queue.title: sy98 model vs the real stale sMarioScreenY ($A23B) register
queue.note: ANSWERED from the ROM 2026-10-13: REFUTED as 'exactly equivalent', but no level-1 decision flips. The port's prev_mario_y_lo is one variable standing in for TWO ROM bytes written at different points - sMarioScreenY ($A23B, written by the draw at main.asm:461-467 per frame) and sPrevMarioY ($A20C, written by the camera body at home.asm:1861-1862). It equals the register on every steady-state free-scroll frame (which is why all 17 captures and the gate pass). It differs in: (a) the first frame after $0F2A, where the register holds the constant $40 (home.asm:2095) while the port computes sy98 (for level 1: $76 vs $40 - both below the $90 down-lock read, so same decision, but a level whose spawn arithmetic lands >= $90 would arm a down transition the console would not); (b) every frame while sScreenTransition != 0 (the ROM's draw keeps refreshing the register from the walked Mario position; the port returns before its latch, so its proxy freezes and ends the transition stale by tens of px); (c) parked frames (scene/boss). None of the stale values is CONSULTED in level 1: the register is read only at the $C0 down-lock (home.asm:1722) and the $48 up-lock (home.asm:1782), which the transition ends never straddle with a stale latch. The genuinely reachable hit is on the OTHER half of the same conflation: after an UP transition the ROM rewrites $FFC0 = 0 and latches sPrevMarioY = 0, while the port keeps prev_mario_y_lo = the pre-warp Y, so dv can land on opposite sides of $80 - i.e. the up/down BRANCH itself can differ after an up transition via the y_lo=$48 + bit2 + sMarioScreenY < $1B arm, which level 1's table enables (bit2 in cells 16/17/31/46) and the new screen_transition1 capture now exercises. Recommendation: keep the sy98 model (right on every consulted frame) and test the up-transition dv case against screen_transition1 before changing anything.

queue.title: sMapScrollLimit: --play leaves it false while run_replay seeds it from the capture
queue.verification_gate: cargo test + the 18-capture gate (level 1 is unaffected: both bytes are $00)
queue.note: DONE 2026-10-13. --play now seeds both flags from the manifest's per-level property table instead of running on the defaults: `cam.map_scroll_limit = manifest.properties.unknown != 0` and `cam.auto_scroll = manifest.properties.auto_scroll` (sMapScrollLimit is a bool test of a nonzero byte, but sAutoScroll keeps the byte itself - it is read for `!= 0` at home.asm:1533-1537). Same shape of gap as the edge map: run_replay took both from its capture's frame 0 while the play path had no source at all. Level 1 is $00 in both and all 16 original captures record limit=false/autoscroll=0, so the 18-capture gate is unchanged. ROM: sMapScrollLimit ($A2D9) has exactly ONE writer, the state-$03 level-load handler $04F1 at home.asm:741-747 ('ld hl, LevelPropertiesUNK / ld a,[sCurLevel] / ... / ld [sMapScrollLimit],a'), so it is a per-level constant from LevelPropertiesUNK (home.asm:4087-4091); LevelPropertiesScroll (home.asm:4093-4097) -> sAutoScroll at home.asm:633-639 and LevelPropertiesSpace (home.asm:4099-4103) -> sMoonPhysics at home.asm:655-661 do the same for the other flags. The manifest already carries all three (level.rs:200-209). The 12 levels with a nonzero limit byte are 0-based indices 2,3,4,5,6,10,15,18,19,24,28,31 (all $08); autoscroll levels are 19, 25, 30 - those three now print the not-modelled note in play mode too, since $0DAF is still unported.

queue.title: Autoscroll camera path ($0DAF) is unmodelled
queue.note: DESCRIBED from the ROM 2026-10-13, and it is small - the port already has every piece. $0B2A's dispatcher (home.asm:1533-1537) sends sAutoScroll != 0 to $0DAF instead of the whole horizontal block; the vertical follow ($0C7D) and the transition machinery are shared unchanged. $0DAF (home.asm:1869-1903) does three things: (1) the right-edge transition trigger, same shape as $0B5E but with >= instead of == (cell edge bit0, cam X lo >= $B0, sMarioScreenX >= $A1 -> sScreenTransition = 1 + the $0F0B scene latch); (2) otherwise return unless $FF97 is EVEN ('ldh a,[$FF97] / and $01 / ret nz') - so the scroll is 1 px per TWO frames; (3) on even frames clear sScrollLeftEnabled and add 1 to cam X lo (carry into $FFCB, masked $0F), setting sMapScrollFlags bit4. It never applies the player-speed latches, ignores the draw's enables, has no +-1 park correction, no $FF99 pull-back, no left edge lock and no left transition; and because it jumps straight to $0C7D it skips $0C76, so the scroll deltas are not cleared on autoscroll frames. Mario's position is NOT driven by it - he keeps normal physics and drifts toward the left of the screen. Porting: in CameraSim::step, before the vertical block, branch 'if self.auto_scroll != 0 { run_autoscroll(sim) } else { <existing horizontal block> }'; the frame parity is already available (PlayerSim::phase mirrors $FF97 and camera.rs uses it for the down-transition dither). Seed cam.auto_scroll from manifest.properties.auto_scroll in the play-mode setup (run_replay already seeds it at main.rs:965 and prints the not-modelled note at 989-991). No level-1 behaviour changes.

queue.title: START pause + the BGP/OBP0 $E7/$93 flash (16 frames each - a 32-frame cycle off $FF97 bit 4)
queue.verification_gate: cargo test + manual --play check of ENTER/BACKSPACE (no capture can carry START)
queue.note:
DONE 2026-10-13 - core plus the --play wiring. CAVEAT: the interactive path could not be driven in this environment (no key-injection tool: xdotool/ydotool/wtype and grim/scrot/import are all missing), so the window path is verified by construction and by the core tests, not by a capture or a screenshot.
PINNED ROM FACTS: pause is game state $FF9B = 8, not a separate handler - entry stub $273E (home.asm:5181-5194, called at the in-level frame tail from home.asm:818 and the dead branch at 827), handler $2756 (home.asm:5196-5239) via the $08 table entry at home.asm:303. The flash is bit 4 of the global counter $FF97 read EVERY frame ($E7 when clear, $93 when set, home.asm:5197-5201) - a 32-frame cycle off the counter, with no timer and no reload value - and the same byte goes to sBGPalette AND sOAMPalette1 (home.asm:5204-5206); sOAMPalette2/OBP1 is never written. Entry needs hKeysPressed == $08 exactly and sScreenTransition == 0, and the in-level loop zeroes both key bytes while sFadeTimer != 0. Resume is on any frame with the START press bit: it restores the three sLevel* copies ($A80F-$A811) and sets $FF9B = 4. SELECT ($04) with sLevelProgressFlags bit 7 set quits through $FF9B = 20 -> $14. Music pauses via sSoundMode = 1/2 (a held jingle), not sMusicRequest.
PORTED: PlayerKeys gained start/select (the pan's exact-match test now includes both); PlayerSim gained `paused` (the $FF9B = 8 model) and `frame_counter` (the full $FF97 byte - the port kept only `phase`, its low 3 bits, which cannot see bit 4), plus pause_enter/pause_exit/pause_flash/pause_select_exit. --play maps ENTER to START and BACKSPACE to SELECT, tracks both press edges like hKeysPressed, and freezes sim.step/cam.step/obj.step on a paused frame exactly as a fade does - the freeze is read at entry, so the frame START lands on still runs its object pass, because $273E sits at the frame tail. The flash is threaded into the renderer as a BG-palette override plus a per-frame SpriteCtx.obp0 write, so BG and OBJ0 flash together while OBP1 does not; unpaused frames restore the manifest's OBJ0. FLAGGED, not invented: sSoundMode 1/2 (no sound-mode state in the port), sPauseState ($A23D, write-only in the ROM), sMarioDead = 2, sFastMusic; and the ROM's `hKeysPressed == $08` is modelled as 'the START edge on a frame with no fade or transition', since ENTER is not a gameplay key.
TESTS: 4 - the 16/16 flash cadence off bit 4 including both boundaries, enter/exit, the SELECT branch's bit-7 gate with its exit marker, and respawn clearing the pause. cargo test 88; the 18-capture gate is unchanged (no capture carries START, so the replay path passes start:false and the frozen flag stays clear).

queue.title: Scene system: sSceneMap-nonzero levels run a scene at the transition finish (sSceneState = $F0 + the bank-5 script VM $20A4 + the bank-2 $8D9C boss/template set + $8E6C)
queue.note: PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-10-13 (this item, and DESIGN.md, claimed 'state 240' and 'bank-1 $3C94'). 240 is stored into sSceneState (= $F0), NOT $FF9B: the $FF9B jump table ends at $23 (home.asm:330) so 240 could never index it. $3C94 is a bank-0 trampoline to bank 2 $8D9C. Real chain: a hard-edge trigger in $0B2A sets sScreenTransition and calls $0F0B, which latches sSceneId from sSceneMap; when the scroll completes $0EB0 (home.asm:2009-2050) tests sSceneState & $0F and, if nonzero, sets sSceneState = $F0 then calls $3C94 -> $8D9C. Missing from the port: (1) the bank-5 script VM $20A4 (one byte per frame, halt between bytes, 32-entry dw table at $4125 indexed by sSceneId, opcode operand lengths 7/1/0/2/1/0/1/0/0/3 for $0x/$1x/$2x/$3x/$4x/$5x/$6x/$8x/$Ax/$Bx, $FF = END at $21EE); (2) the $0EB0 sSceneState & $0F branch in camera.rs's finish_transition (whose comment says 'bank-1', also wrong); (3) the bank-2 $8D9C path (it does not load VRAM: it clears $AF00-$AFFF and sObjectTable $AD00, then $8DFD builds sObjectDefIndex/sObjectDefCount/sObjectDefSprite, then $8E6C writes 18-byte slot images at a literal $10 stride into $AD25+ - consecutive images OVERLAP by 2 bytes, which is what the ROM arithmetic does, so reproduce it literally); (4) the alternate per-frame driver $8DA9 that REPLACES the normal $8000 engine while sSceneState & $F0 != 0 (selected at home.asm:830-842), with its $92DF anim table, $9048/$505B extents and $3A14 -> bank 19 $6000. sSceneMap extraction mirrors the edge map but from the pointer at [bank:$4002] (home.asm:572-604) -> levelNN.scene.bin; the port's camera.rs scene_lookup already implements the $0F0B index ((MarioYhi & $0F)*16 + (MarioXhi & $0F)) but scene_map is never filled by the runtime, so scene_id is always 0 today. 14 of 32 levels have a nonzero scene map; level 1 is all zeros (re-verified from baserom.gb), which is why no capture touches this. Cleanest first slice: level 3 (level_id 2), whose two scenes are $06 = 40 03 FF and $07 = 40 16 FF - pure 'transition to screen (Y,X)' with no tileset/VRAM/boss/fade work; then level 8 (scenes $01/$02). Full detail in the delegation transcript deleg_52e18705 task-4.

queue.title: Golden coins (sGoldenCoin1-6 $A84D-$A865) and the map-side tally ($307BC / $30884)
queue.note: CONFIRMED with one caveat, 2026-10-13. An exhaustive scan of baserom.gb (every ld [$A84x],a / ld hl,$A84x / ld a,[$A84x] / 16-bit pointer pair / set 7,(hl) site for the six addresses) finds NO in-level writer: the six bytes are written only by (a) $27AF at home.asm:5321-5327 (game over, zeroes all six), (b) the level-clear chain at main.asm:16661-16672 with $304F1 giving levels 5/9/13/16/19/23 the offsets 5/9/$1D/$17/$11/$0E, (c) the map hand-off $3EEF0 (main.asm:24089-24124) via $650E for the six coin nodes, and (d) the SRAM load. So the port's 'no in-level writer' note holds. CAVEAT: the corollary 'c is always 0' is NOT a general invariant - it holds only for a save with no coin-level progress; once any of the six coin levels is completed the corresponding byte is set and $27AF's BCD subtract is nonzero. Also: sGoldenCoinCount never feeds the level-clear tally (that is +1 BCD per newly cleared level, coin-independent); the only tally/coin interaction is the game-over subtraction.

queue.title: PlayerSim::on_ground_obj is never set true, so every gate that reads sMarioOnObject is inert
queue.note: Found 2026-10-13 while porting the crouch pan. objects.rs computes the on-object/on-ground-cleared result but sml2-runtime only writes on_ground back to PlayerSim, so on_ground_obj stays false forever. Consequences: $307D's '(sMarioOnGround | sMarioOnObject)' gate degenerates to on_ground, and any other reader of sMarioOnObject is equally dead. The $13FE/$134F landing arm in player_sim.rs reads on_ground_obj too. Fixing it means threading the object engine's on-object result into the sim the way on_ground already is, then re-running the gate: a capture where Mario stands on a walker would exercise it.
